definitions.explanation: A deep hole dug into the ground to reach underground water. Traditional wells were common in Japan before modern plumbing.

examples.english: To draw water from a well.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{村|むら}→村：02261_mura⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧{井戸|いど}がある。
examples.english: There is an old well in this village.

examples.japanese: {井戸|いど}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{冷|つめ}たくて→冷たい：00681_tsumetai⟧⟦{美味|おい}しい→美味しい：00740_oishii⟧。
examples.english: Well water is cold and delicious.

notes:
USAGE: In modern Japan, wells are rare in urban areas but still found in rural regions and preserved as cultural heritage.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {井戸|いど}を⟦{掘|ほ}る→掘る：00442_horu⟧ (to dig a well)
- {井戸|いど}⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧ (well water)
- {井戸|いど}⟦{端|ばた}→端：00936_hashi⟧⟦{会議|かいぎ}→会議：00710_kaigi⟧ (gossiping at the well - lit. 'well-side conference')

The expression {井戸|いど}{端|ばた}{会議|かいぎ} refers to casual gossip, historically shared by women gathering at the communal well.
